title: Unifying Grafana and UptimeRobot Webhooks for Unlimited-Seat On‑Call with WakeUp Dev
description: Learn how to combine Grafana and UptimeRobot webhooks to trigger WakeUp Dev alerts, eliminate per‑seat costs, and reduce alert fatigue with voice ACKs.
author: Enrique Drack
topic: Unifying Grafana and UptimeRobot Webhooks for Unlimited-Seat On‑Call with WakeUp Dev

blocks.text: Grafana can send alerts to any HTTP endpoint. Configure the webhook to point at WakeUp Dev's POST /v1/alert endpoint and include your x‑api‑key header.
UptimeRobot also supports webhooks. Use the same endpoint and key so both services funnel into the same on‑call stream.
By routing both Grafana and UptimeRobot alerts through WakeUp Dev you:

items: eliminate per‑seat billing – seats are unlimited
reduce alert fatigue with a single voice ACK workflow
keep all alert metadata in one place for audit and analysis

blocks.code:
curl -X POST https://api.wakeupdev.com/v1/alert \
  -H \"x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{
  \"source\": \"grafana\",
  \"severity\": \"critical\",
  \"title\": \"CPU usage > 90%\",
  \"message\": \"Instance i-1234 is over 90% CPU.\",
  \"tags\": [\"cpu\", \"production\"]
}'

blocks.text: The response will trigger a voice cascade to the on‑call roster. The first person to press 1 acknowledges the alert, ending the call for the rest.
